class.name: MultiMesh
class.brief_description: Provides high-performance drawing of a mesh multiple times using GPU instancing.
class.description: MultiMesh provides low-level mesh instancing. Drawing thousands of [MeshInstance3D] nodes can be slow, since each object is submitted to the GPU then drawn individually. MultiMesh is much faster as it can draw thousands of instances with a single draw call, resulting in less API overhead. As a drawback, if the instances are too far away from each other, performance may be reduced as every single instance will always render (they are spatially indexed as one, for the whole object). Since instances may have any behavior, the AABB used for visibility must be provided by the user. [b]Note:[/b] A MultiMesh is a single object, therefore the same maximum lights per object restriction applies. This means, that once the maximum lights are consumed by one or more instances, the rest of the MultiMesh instances will [b]not[/b] receive any lighting. [b]Note:[/b] Blend Shapes will be ignored if used in a MultiMesh.

link.title: Animating thousands of fish with MultiMeshInstance

method.name: pack_transform_buffer
method.description: Cgame extension: returns a packed GPU-ready instance buffer from an array of [Transform3D] values and optional colors. This CPU-only method does not modify the MultiMesh or upload data to the renderer. The current MultiMesh must use [constant TRANSFORM_3D], have an [member instance_count] matching the array length, and have [member use_custom_data] disabled. If [member use_colors] is enabled, provide exactly one color per transform; otherwise pass an empty [PackedColorArray]. Every transform uses the RenderingServer 3D row-major layout (12 floats per instance), followed by four RGBA color floats when enabled. Invalid inputs yield an empty buffer and log an error. Assign the result to [member buffer] once after validating inputs. This is intended for large static scenery batches created during world streaming, not dynamic per-frame animation.

method.name: transformed_mesh_bounds
method.description: Cgame extension: returns the union of the current [member mesh]'s [method Mesh.get_aabb] after applying each provided [Transform3D], expanded by the nonnegative [param margin] on all sides. This CPU-only method has no rendering-server calls and is suitable for [member MultiMeshInstance3D.custom_aabb]. A conservative transformed bound is essential because a MultiMesh is frustum-culled as a single object, not per instance. Requires a valid mesh, at least one transform and a finite nonnegative margin.

method.name: reset_instance_physics_interpolation
method.description: When using [i]physics interpolation[/i], this function allows you to prevent interpolation on an instance in the current physics tick. This allows you to move instances instantaneously, and should usually be used when initially placing an instance such as a bullet to prevent graphical glitches.

method.name: reset_instances_physics_interpolation
method.description: When using [i]physics interpolation[/i], this function allows you to prevent interpolation for all instances in the current physics tick. This allows you to move all instances instantaneously, and should usually be used when initially placing instances to prevent graphical glitches.

method.name: shuffled_instance_buffer
method.description: Returns a new buffer containing the same instance records in a seeded random order, without modifying [param buffer] or uploading anything to the rendering device. Each record's transform, color, and optional custom data are moved together. This makes an evenly shuffled prefix suitable for distance-dependent [member visible_instance_count] with no missing spatial rows. The current [member transform_format], [member use_colors], [member use_custom_data], and [member instance_count] determine the packed record stride. If the buffer length is not exactly compatible with the instance count and stride, the input is returned unchanged. The seed uses Godot's [RandomNumberGenerator] PCG sequence, matching a Fisher-Yates shuffle from the final record to the second record with [method RandomNumberGenerator.randi_range] between index 0 and the current index. Use the returned array as [member buffer] once after instance allocation; do not invoke this helper every render frame. This engine extension also supports 2D instances.

method.name: set_buffer_interpolated
method.description: An alternative to setting the [member buffer] property, which can be used with [i]physics interpolation[/i]. This method takes two arrays, and can set the data for the current and previous tick in one go. The renderer will automatically interpolate the data at each frame. This is useful for situations where the order of instances may change from physics tick to tick, such as particle systems. When the order of instances is coherent, the simpler alternative of setting [member buffer] can still be used with interpolation.

method.name: set_instance_colors_batch
method.description: Sets colors for selected MultiMesh instances using one scripting call. [member use_colors] must be enabled. The arrays must be equally sized, indices must be unique and within [member instance_count], and all RGBA components must be finite. Unsorted and hidden indices are allowed. The complete input is checked before any changes; invalid input returns [code]false[/code] without modifying any instance, and a valid empty input returns [code]true[/code]. Updates neither [member instance_count] nor [member visible_instance_count], transforms, custom shader data, or collision. This reduces script-to-engine overhead for sparse updates and initial chunk tint population. Internally each instance still requires a RenderingServer color update; it is not a GPU batch command. For full-buffer updates use [member buffer].

method.name: set_instance_color
method.description: Sets the color of a specific instance by [i]multiplying[/i] the mesh's existing vertex colors. This allows for different color tinting per instance. [b]Note:[/b] Each component is stored in 32 bits in the Forward+ and Mobile rendering methods, but is packed into 16 bits in the Compatibility rendering method. For the color to take effect, ensure that [member use_colors] is [code]true[/code] on the [MultiMesh] and [member BaseMaterial3D.vertex_color_use_as_albedo] is [code]true[/code] on the material. If you intend to set an absolute color instead of tinting, make sure the material's albedo color is set to pure white ([code]Color(1, 1, 1)[/code]).

method.name: set_instance_custom_data
method.description: Sets custom data for a specific instance. [param custom_data] is a [Color] type only to contain 4 floating-point numbers. [b]Note:[/b] Each number is stored in 32 bits in the Forward+ and Mobile rendering methods, but is packed into 16 bits in the Compatibility rendering method. For the custom data to be used, ensure that [member use_custom_data] is [code]true[/code]. This custom instance data has to be manually accessed in your custom shader using [code]INSTANCE_CUSTOM[/code].

method.name: set_instance_transforms_batch
method.description: Updates sparse 3D instance transforms with one scripting call. Requires [enum TRANSFORM_3D], equally sized arrays, unique indices within [member instance_count], and finite transforms. All entries are validated before any updates. Invalid inputs return [code]false[/code] and leave the buffer unchanged, including all other instance slots. An empty valid request returns [code]true[/code], and hidden slots may also be updated. This does not change [member instance_count], [member visible_instance_count], colors, custom data, collision, or game entity IDs. One RenderingServer command is still issued per instance. For dense updates use [member buffer]; this API is not a single GPU upload.

method.name: set_instance_transform_color_buffer
method.description: Validates and uploads the complete array of 3D instance transforms and instance RGBA colors using one packed MultiMesh buffer update. This combines native packing with a single RenderingServer full-buffer upload; it does not send a separate update for every instance. The MultiMesh must have [enum TRANSFORM_3D], [member use_colors] enabled and [member use_custom_data] disabled. Both arrays must have exactly [member instance_count] elements, every transform must be [Transform3D], and every transform/color component must be finite. Invalid input returns [code]false[/code] without changing the existing buffer. Zero instances with empty input is valid. The method uses 16 packed float values per instance (a row-major 3x4 transform and four RGBA floats). This [b]replaces all instance transform and color values[/b], including hidden slots; [member instance_count], [member visible_instance_count] and the mesh stay unchanged. It does not update collision, navigation or game entity IDs. Prefer this method when initializing an entire dense 3D batch from gameplay data. For sparse updates, use [method set_instance_transforms_batch] and [method set_instance_colors_batch] instead. Regular Godot can achieve the same buffer layout with [member buffer].

method.name: set_instance_transform
method.description: Sets the [Transform3D] for a specific instance.

method.name: set_instance_transform_2d
method.description: Sets the [Transform2D] for a specific instance.

method.name: activate_hidden_instances
method.description: Activates multiple hidden instances in an existing MultiMesh buffer without changing [member instance_count]. Indices refer to the [b]original hidden slots[/b] at the start of the call; their order in [param hidden_instances] does not matter. The method validates all indices, rejects duplicates and already-visible or out-of-bounds indices, sorts the copy, then activates each in ascending order so the intended complete payloads are preserved. Returns the number activated, [code]0[/code] for an empty array, or [code]-1[/code] for invalid input without changing any instances. Works with a partial visible prefix (including [code]0[/code]); when [member visible_instance_count] is [code]-1[/code], all instances are visible, so any nonempty request fails. This method preserves paired transforms, optional colors and shader custom data through [method activate_hidden_instance]. It never changes memory allocation, physics collision, navigation or entity IDs. After activation the ordering of hidden slots may change; game code is responsible for persistent entity IDs and restoring original payloads if needed. [b]Performance:[/b] Validation and sorting cost [code]O(K log K)[/code] and activation uses [code]K[/code] individual rendering server operations. It reduces scripting API crossings but is not a single GPU command.

method.name: activate_hidden_instance
method.description: Reactivates one currently hidden MultiMesh instance without allocating a new buffer. It swaps the complete payload (transform, optional color and shader custom data) from [param hidden_instance] into the first hidden slot, then increases [member visible_instance_count] by one. The instance count is unchanged. It resets physics interpolation for moved slots. If [member visible_instance_count] is [code]-1[/code], all instances are already visible and this call returns [code]false[/code]. The method also returns [code]false[/code] for indices outside the allocated buffer or indices that are already in the visible prefix, without modifying state. An empty buffer has no hidden slots. Use [method remove_visible_instance] to free an active slot first or allocate a larger buffer using [member instance_count]. [b]Important:[/b] This is a low-level instance-pooling primitive. It does not restore a game entity's persistent ID, physics collision, or original transform automatically. Game code must track stable IDs and restore the desired payload to the chosen hidden instance before calling. When an instance is activated from a different hidden slot, hidden slot order changes.

method.name: remove_visible_instances
method.description: Removes multiple currently visible instance indices from the active prefix, without changing [member instance_count]. The list may be unsorted; this method validates every index, rejects duplicates, then performs swap-removal from the [b]highest original index to the lowest[/b], preserving the requested set of removals. It copies and sorts the list internally. Returns the number of instances removed, [code]0[/code] for an empty array, or [code]-1[/code] if any index is invalid, hidden, or repeated. Invalid input causes [b]no[/b] modifications. When [member visible_instance_count] is [code]-1[/code], all allocated instances are initially visible. Optional instance color and shader data are transferred together with their transforms. [b]Important:[/b] Slot indices of surviving instances may change after removal. Track stable gameplay IDs separately. This call only changes rendering state; game collision and navigation must be handled elsewhere. The batch validates and sorts indices in [code]O(K log K)[/code] time and performs [code]K[/code] individual renderer updates. It reduces script API crossings and safely handles unordered input, but does [b]not[/b] submit a single GPU batch command.

method.name: remove_visible_instance
method.description: Removes one currently visible instance from the active prefix without resizing the [MultiMesh] buffer. This is a constant-time swap-removal: the last visible instance's complete payload (transform, optional color and custom data) replaces the removed slot, then [member visible_instance_count] decreases by one. The actual [member instance_count] remains unchanged. If [member visible_instance_count] is [code]-1[/code], all allocated instances are initially considered visible. Removing the final visible instance sets the visible count to [code]0[/code], not [code]-1[/code]. Returns [code]false[/code] for a negative index, an index outside the currently visible prefix, or when no instances remain, without changing the buffer or its visibility. [b]Important:[/b] This method does not preserve the order or stable IDs of visible instances. Maintain a separate mapping between game entity IDs and buffer indices if they must survive removal or serialization. Physics interpolation is reset for swapped slots via [method swap_instance_data]. [b]Note:[/b] This operation does not affect collision objects, navigation data or higher-level game entities. It removes the instance only from rendering.

method.name: swap_instance_data
method.description: Swaps the complete payload of two instances: their [Transform3D] or [Transform2D], instance color (if [member use_colors] is enabled), and per-instance custom data (if [member use_custom_data] is enabled). Returns [code]true[/code] on success; invalid indices return [code]false[/code] without changing any instance. Passing the same index twice succeeds without modifying anything. This method can be used for constant-time, order-independent removal from an active prefix: swap the unwanted index with the last visible slot, then decrease [member visible_instance_count]. The method itself does [b]not[/b] change the instance count, visible count, or persistent game entity IDs. It resets physics interpolation of the swapped slots to avoid visual trails. [b]Note:[/b] In-memory slot indices are not persistent entity identifiers when swap-removal is used. Maintain a separate mapping from stable game IDs to current indices. This helper does not perform culling, collision or allocation changes.

member.deprecated: Accessing this property is very slow. Use [method set_instance_color] and [method get_instance_color] instead.

Custom AABB for this MultiMesh resource. Setting this manually prevents costly runtime AABB recalculations.

member.name: custom_data_array
member.deprecated: Accessing this property is very slow. Use [method set_instance_custom_data] and [method get_instance_custom_data] instead.

members.member: Array containing each custom data value used by all instances of this mesh, as a [PackedColorArray].

Number of instances that will get drawn. This clears and (re)sizes the buffers. Setting data format or flags afterwards will have no effect. By default, all instances are drawn but you can limit this with [member visible_instance_count].
[Mesh] resource to be instanced. The looks of the individual instances can be modified using [method set_instance_color] and [method set_instance_custom_data].

Choose whether to use an interpolation method that favors speed or quality. When using low physics tick rates (typically below 20) or high rates of object rotation, you may get better results from the high quality setting. [b]Note:[/b] Fast quality does not equate to low quality. Except in the special cases mentioned above, the quality should be comparable to high quality.

member.name: transform_2d_array
member.deprecated: Accessing this property is very slow. Use [method set_instance_transform_2d] and [method get_instance_transform_2d] instead.

members.member: Array containing each [Transform2D] value used by all instances of this mesh, as a [PackedVector2Array]. Each transform is divided into 3 [Vector2] values corresponding to the transforms' [code]x[/code], [code]y[/code], and [code]origin[/code].

member.name: transform_array
member.deprecated: Accessing this property is very slow. Use [method set_instance_transform] and [method get_instance_transform] instead.

members.member: Array containing each [Transform3D] value used by all instances of this mesh, as a [PackedVector3Array]. Each transform is divided into 4 [Vector3] values corresponding to the transforms' [code]x[/code], [code]y[/code], [code]z[/code], and [code]origin[/code].
Format of transform used to transform mesh, either 2D or 3D.

If [code]true[/code], the [MultiMesh] will use color data (see [method set_instance_color]). Can only be set when [member instance_count] is [code]0[/code] or less. This means that you need to call this method before setting the instance count, or temporarily reset it to [code]0[/code].

If [code]true[/code], the [MultiMesh] will use custom data (see [method set_instance_custom_data]). Can only be set when [member instance_count] is [code]0[/code] or less. This means that you need to call this method before setting the instance count, or temporarily reset it to [code]0[/code].
Limits the number of instances drawn, -1 draws all instances. Changing this does not change the sizes of the buffers.

constants.constant: Always interpolate using Basis lerping, which can produce warping artifacts in some situations.
Attempt to interpolate using Basis slerping (spherical linear interpolation) where possible, otherwise fall back to lerping.
